name: Stream Demote
description: Moves streams that fail for real viewers down the channel's order, so the next tune-in starts on one that works, and keeps them there when other tools re-sort. Watching is passive and uses no provider seats. Includes a flag-as-bad API with its own narrow token, and optional content checks on streams a viewer already has open.
author: Kurrt

fields.label: Start here
fields.help_text: Dry run is on, so nothing moves until you turn it off. Read the journal first: Export journal shows what it would have done.

fields.label: Dry run
fields.help_text: Log what it would do and change nothing, including restores and putting streams back after another tool. Undo buttons still work. Turn this off when the journal looks right.

fields.label: When a stream is demoted
fields.help_text: A stream is demoted when its score reaches the level below, adding up failures over the window.

fields.label: Score that demotes
fields.help_text: Raise it to 2 to need two hard failures.

fields.label: Score window (hours)
fields.help_text: Failures older than this stop counting.

fields.label: Weight: hard failure
fields.help_text: Dispatcharr gave up after its retries (reason max_retries_exceeded), soon after the stream started. After the early period it counts as Weight: late stall.

fields.label: Weight: no data or early stall
fields.help_text: No data, or a stall soon after the stream started (reason health_monitor).

fields.label: Weight: late failure
fields.help_text: A stall or hard failure after the early period. Long sessions hiccup, so it counts less.

fields.label: Weight: too slow
fields.help_text: Slower than real time for 15 s (reason buffering_timeout). FFmpeg profiles only.

fields.label: Early period (minutes)
fields.help_text: A stall inside this period counts as early.

fields.label: Hold before acting (seconds)
fields.help_text: Wait this long before judging a failure, so an outage can show itself first.

fields.label: Another stream must play (seconds)
fields.help_text: A stream only drops once another on the channel has delivered data for this long. Otherwise every stream may be bad.

fields.label: Wait for that proof (seconds)
fields.help_text: How long a running channel can take to show it. After this the failure still counts towards the score.

fields.label: Not over-reacting
fields.help_text: These stop one bad evening rewriting your channels.

fields.label: Proof a provider is up (seconds)
fields.help_text: Another stream on the account that keeps playing this long proves the provider is up.

fields.label: Outage: failed streams
fields.help_text: This many failed streams on one account, on at least two channels, with nothing else playing there, is an outage.

fields.label: Outage: window (seconds)
fields.help_text: Failures this far apart can count as one outage.

fields.label: Outage: pause (minutes)
fields.help_text: No demotions on that account for this long after an outage.

fields.label: Outage: give up after (hours)
fields.help_text: After this long the account counts as broken, not out, and demotions go ahead. 0 means never.

fields.label: Outage: undo recent (minutes)
fields.help_text: When an outage is seen, demotions made this recently on that account are undone.

fields.label: Follow-on failure (seconds)
fields.help_text: Another stream on the account failing this close is treated as a possible outage until it happens again.

fields.label: Stall guard (seconds)
fields.help_text: Failures this soon after a stall on the account don't count: the old connection can still hold the seat.

fields.label: Zap guard (seconds)
fields.help_text: Failures on a stream tried this soon after another channel on the account stopped don't count, even with no limit set in Dispatcharr.

fields.label: Let off at most (spells)
fields.help_text: After failing this many separate times, 10 minutes or more apart, under those two guards, a stream's failure counts anyway. 0 means never.

fields.label: All streams failed (minutes)
fields.help_text: If every stream on a channel failed within this time, the order is left alone.

fields.label: Limit: per channel in a burst
fields.help_text: Most demotions on one channel in the burst window.

fields.label: Limit: everything per hour
fields.help_text: Above this it stops demoting and warns you.

fields.label: Channels to leave alone
fields.help_text: Comma-separated channel numbers, ranges such as 9000-9999, or channel group names. Nothing here moves their streams: no demotion, no second chance, no earning back and no putting back after another tool. Undo buttons still work.

fields.label: Earn back by playing (minutes)
fields.help_text: A demoted stream that plays this long without failing goes back where it was.

fields.label: Second chance after (hours)
fields.help_text: A demoted stream goes back for another try after this long. The wait doubles each time it fails again. 0 means never.

fields.label: Second chance after a flag (hours)
fields.help_text: The same, for a stream a person flagged: a person saw it, so it waits longer. Never shorter than the one above.

fields.label: Other tools that sort streams
fields.help_text: Tools such as Stream-Mapparr and Lineuparr rewrite a channel's order. This puts demoted streams back at the bottom afterwards, and leaves the rest of that tool's order alone. A hand reorder or an Undo sticks.

fields.label: Keep demotions when other tools re-sort
fields.help_text: Compares channels with active demotions with how they were left.

fields.label: Wait for it to settle (seconds)
fields.help_text: A changed order must hold still this long first, so a tool still working isn't raced.

fields.label: Most times per channel per hour
fields.help_text: Above this it stops on that channel for the hour and warns you, so two tools can't fight for ever.

fields.label: Forget a removed stream after (minutes)
fields.help_text: A demoted stream that has left the channel for this long is forgotten. If it comes back it starts clean.

fields.label: Content checks
fields.help_text: Off by default. Looks at a few seconds of what Dispatcharr already holds for a stream a viewer has open, with ffmpeg, using no provider connection. See the README.

fields.label: Check content
fields.help_text: The off switch for everything in this section.

fields.label: Skip content checks on
fields.help_text: Channel numbers, ranges such as 9000-9999, or channel group names, comma-separated. For event and part-time channels that show a slate between events. Failures still count there as usual; only the picture and sound checks are skipped.

fields.label: No audio track
fields.help_text: Channels with no video at all are radio, and are always skipped.

fields.label: Placeholder pictures and files
fields.help_text: A picture seen on several channels, or one you taught it, or a fixed-length file on an FFmpeg-style profile. Only picture fingerprints are kept.

fields.label: Count a still picture when there is sound
fields.help_text: A black or frozen picture with sound playing has to last twice as long. Turn off to never count it, for channels that show a card over music.

fields.label: Act on content checks (experimental)
fields.help_text: Off: a failed check is only written to the journal as content_failed. On: it counts as a failure and can move the viewer. Tests found good streams demoted, so read the README first.

fields.label: Move the viewer on
fields.help_text: Switch to the next stream when a check fails, if the viewer is still there.

fields.label: Bad samples needed
fields.help_text: In a row. Never fewer than 2.

fields.label: Over at least (seconds)
fields.help_text: So a dark scene or a quiet moment doesn't count.

fields.label: Give up on a check after (seconds)
Placeholder: seen on this many channels
Teach from channel
fields.help_text: Channel number used by the Teach a placeholder button. Someone must be watching it.

fields.label: Flag button
fields.help_text: See the README before using these.

fields.label: Move to the next stream on a flag
fields.help_text: Switch the running session to the next stream straight away, if a viewer is still there.

fields.label: Weight: flag
fields.help_text: How much a flag counts in a stream's record, which decides the order of demoted streams at the bottom. A hard failure counts 1.

fields.label: Flag limit: per channel (seconds)
fields.help_text: One flag per channel in this time.

fields.label: Flag limit: per token per hour
Token label
fields.help_text: Name for a new token, or the label to revoke, such as living-room-tv.

fields.label: Channel to undo
fields.help_text: Channel number used by the Undo a channel button.

fields.label: Write a shared event
fields.help_text: Adds a stream_demoted row to System Events, which a stats plugin can read.

actions.label: Event handler
actions.description: Runs by itself on these events. The button does nothing.

actions.label: Status
actions.description: Mode, route and the last 24 hours.

actions.label: Export journal
actions.description: Writes every recent move to a CSV file and shows the last five.

actions.label: Undo a channel
actions.description: Reverses every demotion on the channel in Channel to undo.

actions.label: Undo everything
actions.description: Reverses every demotion still in the journal.

confirm.title: Undo every demotion?
confirm.message: Every demoted stream goes back to where it was.

actions.label: Create a flag token
actions.description: Uses Token label. The token can only flag a channel that is playing.

actions.label: Revoke a token
actions.description: Revokes the token named in Token label.

actions.label: Teach a placeholder
actions.description: Remembers the still picture the channel in Teach from channel is showing now, as a fingerprint.

actions.label: Forget placeholders
actions.description: Forgets every remembered picture, taught or seen.

actions.label: Erase plugin data
actions.description: Clears the journal, tokens and history. Leaves stream order alone.

confirm.title: Erase plugin data?
confirm.message: Undo will no longer be possible for past demotions, and all tokens stop working.
